title: Rice-VL: Evaluating Vision-Language Models for Cultural Understanding Across ASEAN Countries
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the models' ability to answer visual questions (culturalVQA) and localize visual elements (visual grounding) related to the cultural domains of 'Religious Practices' and 'Places of Worship' across 11 Southeast Asian countries. This included identifying religious artifacts, festivals (e.g., Thaipusam), customs (e.g., Morning Alm Rounds), and structures (e.g., temples).
findings: Models demonstrated lower accuracy in grounding abstract cultural elements, including those related to 'Religious Practices', compared to categories with more prominent visual features. Models trained on culturally rich datasets were better at pinpointing region-specific religious artifacts and structures compared to general-purpose models.
